sentences.text:
Ajmer Singh And Another
 ...Petitioners
 Versus
State Of Haryana And Another
 ...Respondents
Coram:
Hon'Ble
Mr. Justice N. S. Shekhawat

Present: Mr. Manoj Kumar Taya, Advocate
 for the petitioners (through V.C.).
 Mr. Rajinder Kumar Banku, Dag, Haryana.

Mr. Sandeep Singh Rana, Advocate
 for respondent No.2 (through V.C.).
 *

***
N. S. Shekhawat, J. (Oral)

1 .  The instant petition has been filed under Section under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing of an FIR No. 151 dated 01.06.2023 under Sections 34, 406, 420 and 506 IPC and Section 24 of the Immigration Act registered at Police Station Nissing, District Karnal,
(Annexure P-1) alongwith all the consequential proceedings arising therefrom on the basis of compromise dated 17.10.2023 (Annexure P-2).
2.
A status report by way of an affidavit of the Deputy Superintendent of Police, Assandh, District Karnal has been filed on behalf of the respondent No.1-State and the same is taken on record.

3. Vide order dated 30.05.2024 while issuing notice of motion, by a Co-ordinate Bench of this Court had directed the parties to appear before the Illaqa Magistrate/trial Magistrate for getting their statements recorded with respect to the compromise dated 17.10.2023 (Annexure P-2).

sentences.text:
Pursuant to aforesaid order, the parties have appeared before the Judicial Magistrate First Class,
Karnal and got their statements recorded.

Report 1 of 2 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:120323 dated 30.07.2024 has been received whereby after recording the statements of the parties, the Court below has shown its satisfaction that the compromise is genuine, voluntary and without any coercion or undue influence.
5. I have heard counsel for the parties and gone through the case file.

6. In the light of the satisfaction shown by the Court below and considering the offence for which the accused have been charged are not of serious nature, together with the fact that compromise will go a long way in ironing out the differences for betterment of future life of the parties and also in view of the law laid down in Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab and another, 2012 (4) RCR (Criminal) 543 and Kulwinder Singh and others Vs. State of Punjab 2007(3) RCR (Criminal) 1052, the present petition for quashing the FIR is allowed qua the petitioners.
